tasks.short: Monitor semiconductor processing and adjust controls

steps.what: Monitor operation and adjust processing machine controls for the required electronic properties

tasks.design: Keep live process monitoring and adjustment with the processor using {OTHER}, the equipment-control terminal. Consult the controlled lot instructions in {OPS_SYSTEM} during that work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual process conditions need interpretation before controls are adjusted.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing equipment controls support operation; no new process-control retrofit is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising abnormal conditions and preserving the intended material properties.
tasks.human_edge: The processor checks actual behaviour against the intended process and escalates uncertainty.

reach.task: Explain operating limits and deviation handling

evidence.claim: Critical Manufacturing MES supports semiconductor recipe rules and equipment links; that capability does not establish a new saving in live operator adjustment.

assumptions: Boundary is actual monitoring and adjustment, not a separate process-reporting task.

Equipment produces readings and process engineer supplies controlled instructions; processor checks lot identity, recipe version, units and actual condition during s1. No free correct-composition or safe-adjustment flag is assumed.
Use existing controls first; existing automatic equipment runtime is not human effort.
Incremental upkeep is zero because no new controller or data feed is introduced.
research_questions: Which interventions require direct observation rather than another dashboard?

already_counted.description: Live monitoring, contextual checks and adjustment

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross and net saving. Live adjustment retains its time and current machine runtime earns no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count, sort and weigh processed items

steps.what: Count, sort and weigh processed items while preserving lot identity and handling requirements

tasks.design: Retain physical counting, sorting and weighing with the processor. Use {OTHER}, the existing counting and weighing equipment, within the current handling process.
tasks.previous_blocker: The items must be physically handled and kept associated with the correct lot.
tasks.enabler_now: Current measuring equipment supports the work; no automated handling retrofit is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Fragile items, mixed lots, uncertain counts and discrepancies between instructions and actual material.
tasks.human_edge: The processor notices handling and identity problems before items move onward.

reach.task: Confirm lot transfer and handling instructions

evidence.claim: Physical item handling is not removed by manufacturing records software; no counting or sorting retrofit is established by this digest.

assumptions: Boundary is physical counting, sorting and weighing, not a separate record-compilation task.
Processor produces actual counts and weights during s1 and checks lot identity and sorting instructions. No free structured count, weight or discrepancy code is assumed.
Use existing counting and weighing capability first; current instrument runtime earns no human saving.
Incremental upkeep is zero because no new automated handling system is introduced.
research_questions: Which portions of handling require manual intervention despite existing measuring equipment?

already_counted.description: Physical count, sorting, weighing and identity checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross and net saving. Physical handling and identity checks retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Calculate etching time from checked process inputs

steps.what: Verify material thickness, target removal and the applicable qualified etching calculation inputs
Calculate etching time with the selected qualified rule and verified material-removal inputs
Check the calculated etching time and resolve missing or out-of-range inputs

tasks.design: Configure the qualified etching-time rule in {OPS_SYSTEM} using inputs verified against the controlled recipe in {DOCS}. Keep applicability, input verification and result checking with the processor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeating arithmetic is distinct from verifying the applicable etch rate and material-removal requirement.
tasks.enabler_now: Native recipe rules can calculate parameters from checked inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Rate validity, material variation, process conditions and operating outside the qualified calculation range.
tasks.human_edge: The processor recognises when the available rate or recipe does not apply.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated arithmetic while retaining process-input checks.

reach.task: Maintain the qualified etch calculation and applicability limits
reach.learn: Which conditions require a new rate determination

evidence.claim: Critical Manufacturing MES supports business-rule recipe parameter calculations for semiconductor manufacturing.
The etching-time saving is an unmeasured scenario and depends on removing actual manual arithmetic.

assumptions: Boundary is calculating and checking time, not performing etching, measuring material again or approving a changed process recipe.

Metrology staff produce identified lot measurements; process engineer produces the qualified rate or calculation and its limits. In s1 the processor obtains and verifies lot and material identifiers, measured and target thickness, removal amount and units, process conditions, applicable rate version and limits. Retrieval and capture are counted in s1.

S2 uses only those checked fields and the selected rule. Missing rate, uncertain units or an out-of-range condition stops for manual engineer resolution in s3; no free valid-rate flag or universal linear-rate assumption is introduced.
Test native recipe configuration first; existing automatic calculation runtime earns no new labour saving.
research_questions: Can native calculations match independent process checks while stopping on invalid applicability conditions?

already_counted.description: Input retrieval, applicability checks and result verification

incremental.description: Maintain calculation checks and review changed recipe-input behaviour
Maintain controlled rule configuration and regression checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+0+30=70; gross 30 minus focal upkeep 8 gives net 22 in an E1 scenario. Range 0-5 allows existing native calculations, sparse manual arithmetic and frequent rate-applicability exceptions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated qualified calculations while retaining live control and physical handling.
reach: Check rate applicability with process engineers
Preserve lot identity during material transfer
role.ambitious_version: A processor with reproducible etching-time calculations who keeps responsibility for actual conditions, handling and exceptions.
